title: Influence of fast and slow laser phase noise on the fidelity of the Mølmer-Sørensen trapped-ion gate
authors: Nikita Semenin, Ksenia Khabarova, Nikolay Kolachevsky
abstract: High-fidelity two-qubit entangling gates are essential for the realization of useful quantum algorithms on quantum processors. The Mølmer-Sørensen (MS) gate has become a common choice for trapped-ion quantum computing due to its resilience to ion temperature and its demonstrated record fidelities. However, the spectral impurity of the driving laser field impacts gate performance, with phase noise influencing the qubit dynamics through mechanisms operating on different timescales. In this work, we present a comprehensive theoretical analysis of laser phase noise in the MS gate, identifying two spectral ranges which influence the gate fidelity the most: "fast" noise at frequencies near the motional mode spectrum, and "slow" noise at frequencies on the order of the inverse gate time. We derive the noise Hamiltonians for two common laser beam geometries and obtain analytical expressions for the average gate error in terms of the laser noise power spectral density and gate parameters. For slowly varying noise spectra, we provide simplified error estimates. In addition, we validate our findings against previously published numerical simulations.
summary: This paper provides a detailed theoretical analysis of how laser phase noise affects the fidelity of the Mølmer-Sørensen gate in trapped-ion quantum computing. The authors derive analytical expressions for the gate error by separating the noise into 'fast' and 'slow' spectral components. This work offers essential quantitative guidelines for improving laser spectral purity in quantum processors.
main_problem: The paper analyzes how laser phase noise degrades the fidelity of the Mølmer-Sørensen (MS) entangling gate used in trapped-ion quantum computing.
main_result: The gate error is shown to be determined by the convolution of the laser noise Power Spectral Density (PSD) with analytically derived filter functions, which are separated into 'fast' and 'slow' noise regimes.
method: The authors perform a comprehensive theoretical analysis, deriving noise Hamiltonians and calculating the average gate error using the Dyson series formalism, leading to analytical expressions for the error.
model_or_system: The system is trapped-ion quantum computing utilizing the Mølmer-Sørensen gate. The analysis models the influence of intrinsic laser phase noise on the qubit dynamics.
key_observables: Gate Fidelity and the average gate error ($\epsilon$).
important_parameters: Laser noise Power Spectral Density (PSD), gate time ($	au$), and spectral frequency ranges ('fast' near motional spectrum, 'slow' near inverse gate time).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the noise is intrinsic phase noise of the common laser source, and it utilizes approximations valid in the Lamb-Dicke regime.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the MS gate level scheme with four Raman paths, and Figure 2 shows how the laser field PSD overlaps with system energy levels, distinguishing between 'slow' and 'fast' noise components.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the MS gate and the source of noise, to deriving the noise Hamiltonians for different geometries, calculating the error using the Dyson series, and finally presenting analytical expressions for the error in both fast and slow noise regimes.
why_interesting: This work provides crucial, detailed analytical tools for quantifying decoherence sources specific to trapped-ion quantum gates, which is vital for designing fault-tolerant quantum hardware.
